title: The Risk of Sanitary Tees on Horizontal Drain Lines
description: Using a standard sanitary tee in a horizontal-to-horizontal waste line transition is a common mistake in drainage installations. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for vertical-to-horizontal flow transitions. When installed horizontally, the short sweep fails to direct wastewater smoothly in the direction of flow, leading to frequent solids buildup, sluggish drainage, and potential backflow into adjoining fixtures. To maintain proper flow velocity and prevent clogs, horizontal branch connections should always use a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-sweep turn fitting, adhering to local plumbing codes.

The Risk of Sanitary Tees on Horizontal Drain Lines

Using a standard sanitary tee in a horizontal-to-horizontal waste line transition is a common mistake in drainage installations. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for vertical-to-horizontal flow transitions. When installed horizontally, the short sweep fails to direct wastewater smoothly in the direction of flow, leading to frequent solids buildup, sluggish drainage, and potential backflow into adjoining fixtures. To maintain proper flow velocity and prevent clogs, horizontal branch connections should always use a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-sweep turn fitting, adhering to local plumbing codes.
